headline: Big Bear Mountain Road and Lake Use Requirements
reservation: Separate reservations are required for commercial lodging, mountain resort lift tickets, and specific boat dock slips. During winter, Snow Valley and Big Bear Mountain Resort often require advance pass purchases. Lake use requires a Quagga Mussel inspection and a permit for private vessels; always verify current traction laws and forest closure status via official Caltrans and USFS channels before travel.

days.title: Lake Views and Village Life
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Big Bear Village

stops.name: Alpine Pedal Path
stops.detail: A paved route along the north shore suitable for walking and cycling with clear lake vistas.

stops.name: Big Bear Village
stops.detail: Explore the walkable mountain town center for local dining and artisan shops.

days.driving: Local travel under 20 minutes; allow for slow weekend traffic in the Village.
days.note: Pedal Path accessibility depends on seasonal snow clearance.

days.title: Forest Heights and Scenic Vistas

stops.name: Castle Rock Trail
stops.detail: A steep ascent through granite boulders providing panoramic views of the water.

stops.name: Stanfield Marsh Wildlife and Nature Preserve
stops.detail: Walk the wooden boardwalks to observe waterfowl in their natural mountain habitat.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes to circle the lake; conditions vary with weather.
days.note: Castle Rock parking is limited to designated turnouts; avoid blocking traffic.

days.title: Summit Activities and Slope Scenery

stops.name: Big Bear Mountain Resort
stops.detail: Visit for winter skiing or summer mountain biking and scenic sky chair rides.

stops.name: Boulder Bay Park
stops.detail: A picturesque shoreline spot featuring large rock formations and picnic areas.

days.driving: Allow 15-20 minutes between the resort and the bay.
days.note: Resort activity availability is strictly weather-dependent; check official snow reports.

intel.title: Adventure Pass Requirements
intel.text: Parking at National Forest trailheads often requires a National Forest Adventure Pass. Purchase these at local mountain stores before heading to remote trailheads.

intel.title: Mountain Topography
intel.text: Expect reliable signal in the Village and Big Bear City. Remote forest roads on the north side frequently experience total signal loss.

intel.title: Gateway Supply
intel.text: Fuel up in San Bernardino or Redlands before beginning the ascent. While stations exist in town, mountain prices are typically higher.

intel.title: Weekend Congestion
intel.text: Sunday afternoon traffic descending the mountain via Highway 18 can add hours to travel. Plan an early morning or late evening departure to avoid peak volume.

intel.title: Winter Traction
intel.text: Caltrans may mandate tire chains on all non-AWD vehicles during active snowfall. Always carry chains in your vehicle from November through April.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at San Bernardino (SBD). Drive Highway 330/18 up the mountain and check into your cabin before dark to navigate winding roads easily.
plan.vehicle: AWD is recommended for winter; check rental restrictions regarding snow chain installation on new vehicles.
plan.goldenHour: Boulder Bay Park provides a popular vista for sunset, though winter shadows fall early in the canyon.
